Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.seal

Class LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.seal.LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator extends Object implements Serializable
Gas leakage through a straight-through labyrinth seal (teeth on stator).

The calculator takes any NeqSim fluid, the upstream pressure and temperature, the downstream pressure (or the pressure drop) and a LabyrinthSealGeometry, and returns the leakage mass flow with the selected LabyrinthFlowMethod. Upstream gas properties (density, molar mass and the real-gas isentropic exponent kappa = -(Cp/Cv)(v/p)(dp/dv)) come from a TP flash of a clone of the fluid; the caller's fluid is not changed.

With pressures p0 (upstream) and pn (downstream) in kPa, density rho in kg/m3, clearance area A, number of teeth n, radial clearance c, tooth pitch t and tip width b, the methods are:

  • Stodola: m = 0.71 A sqrt(1000 rho (p0^2 - pn^2) / (p0 n))
  • Egli (Aungier coefficients): m = A Cr Ct Cc rho sqrt(1000 R T / M) with contraction ratio Cr = 1 - 1/(3 + (54.3/(1 + 100 c/b))^3.45), throttling coefficient Ct = 2.143 (ln n - 1.464) (1 - pn/p0)^(0.375 pn/p0) / (n - 4.322) and a carry-over coefficient Cc from c/t
  • Vermes: m = u A sqrt(1000 rho p0) sqrt((1 - r^2)/(n + ln r)), r = pn/p0, u = sqrt(1/(1 - alpha)), alpha = 8.52/((t - b)/c + 7.23)
  • Kearton: m = Ck 0.71 A sqrt(1000 p0 rho) sqrt(F (1 - r^2)/n) with Ck = 1 + 3.27 (1 - exp(-0.4 n)) (c/t)^(2/3) and F the mean tooth pressure ratio of the profile p_i = sqrt(p0^2 - (i/n)(p0^2 - pn^2)). The equation peaks at a pressure ratio r*(n) that depends only on the number of teeth (0.43 for two teeth, 0.26 for five); below r* the last tooth is choked and the leakage is held at the peak instead of falling with the backpressure
  • Neumann (modified, teeth on stator): tooth-by-tooth solution of p_{i+1}^2 = p_i^2 - (m/(Cf_i u_i A))^2 p_i/rho_i with a flow coefficient that depends on the tooth pressure ratio, a kinetic carry-over factor after the first tooth and an exact PH flash at the inlet enthalpy after every tooth; see getToothPressures(String). A tooth chokes when its pressure ratio reaches the critical ratio, and the choked leakage is the largest flow at which no tooth chokes.

Each closed-form result is limited to the critical flow of the clearance, m_crit = A sqrt(1000 rho p0 k phi) with phi = (2/(k+1))^((k+1)/(k-1)) (Egli uses the equivalent form A rho sqrt(1000 R T/M) sqrt(k phi)); for Kearton the limit is the lower of this and the Kearton peak. isChoked() reports when a limit is active.

Range problems follow the convention of the differential-pressure flow meters: they never throw. When a correlation is mathematically undefined for the geometry (a non-positive Egli coefficient, or a Vermes residual-energy factor of one or more), that method returns NaN and the reason is listed by getValidityViolations(); isWithinValidityRange() is then false. Invalid inputs (missing values, outlet pressure not below inlet pressure) still throw.

Typical use: 

 LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator calc = new LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator(fluid, geometry);
 calc.setInletPressure(2.765, "barg");
 calc.setInletTemperature(86.12, "C");
 calc.setOutletPressure(1.5417, "barg");
 calc.setMethod(LabyrinthFlowMethod.KEARTON);
 calc.calculate();
 double leakage = calc.getMassFlowRate("kg/hr");

    • computeFlows

      private double[] computeFlows(LabyrinthFlowMethod flowMethod, List<String> violations)
      Computes the uncapped mass flow and the critical mass flow for a method from the stored inlet properties.

      When the correlation is mathematically undefined for the geometry (a non-positive Egli coefficient or a Vermes residual-energy factor of one or more), the uncapped flow is NaN and a message is added to violations.

      Parameters:
      flowMethod - flow method
      violations - list receiving validity violations, each prefixed with the method name
      Returns:
      array {uncapped mass flow, critical mass flow} in kg/s, with an optional third element above zero when the method itself has detected choking (Kearton below its peak pressure ratio)

    • calculate

      public void calculate()
      Runs the selected method.

      Range problems do not throw: when the method is undefined for the geometry the mass flow is NaN and the reason is available from getValidityViolations().

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if inputs are missing or inconsistent, or there is no gas at the inlet

      Kearton pressure factor sqrt(F (1 - r^2) / n), where F is the mean tooth pressure ratio of the profile p_i/p_0 = sqrt(1 - (i/n)(1 - r^2)).

    • keartonCriticalPressureRatio

      static double keartonCriticalPressureRatio(int n)
      Returns the pressure ratio at which the Kearton equation has its maximum leakage. Below this ratio the equation would predict less leakage as the backpressure falls; physically the last tooth is choked and the leakage stays at the peak, which is how LabyrinthFlowMethod.KEARTON is evaluated. The ratio depends only on the number of teeth (for one tooth it is 1/sqrt(3)).
      Parameters:
      n - number of teeth, at least 1
      Returns:
      peak outlet to inlet absolute pressure ratio

    • calculateAllMethods

      public Map<LabyrinthFlowMethod,Double> calculateAllMethods()
      Runs every method on the same inlet state. The calculator keeps the results of the selected method afterwards.

      Every method has a key in the map. A method that is undefined for the geometry maps to NaN and its reason is listed by getValidityViolations(), which after this call covers all methods.

      Returns:
      mass flow in kg/s for each method
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if inputs are missing or inconsistent, or there is no gas at the inlet

      public List<String> getValidityViolations()
      Lists why methods evaluated by the last calculate() or calculateAllMethods() call are outside their correlation range. Each entry starts with the method name. For NEUMANN, a failure of the lazy critical-flow search is added when getCriticalMassFlowRate(String) (also called by toJson()) runs it.
      Returns:
      copy of the list of violations, empty when every evaluated method is within range

    • getCriticalMassFlowRate

      public double getCriticalMassFlowRate(String unit)
      Returns the critical (choked) mass flow of the clearance for the selected method.

      For LabyrinthFlowMethod.NEUMANN this is the largest flow at which no tooth chokes. When the leakage is not choked it is found by a separate search on the first request, which costs additional PH flashes. If that search fails, the result is NaN and the reason is added to getValidityViolations().

      Parameters:
      unit - mass flow unit, see getMassFlowRate(String)
      Returns:
      critical mass flow, NaN when it cannot be determined
